title: Inquest looks at cop's death ; Partner of slain OPP officer seeks closure
article: It's been just more than two years since OPP Const. Vu Pham was shot dead.

It was March 8, 2010, a little past 10 a.m., when 70-year-old Fred Preston, enraged that his wife had left him, blasted a shell from a .270-calibre hunting rifle into Pham's head, killing him instantly.

Monday in London, Ontario's chief coroner begins a dual inquest into the deaths of Pham and Preston. The latter died days after being shot six times by Pham's partner Const. Del Mercey, who was in a separate cruiser.
Ontario's Special Investigation Unit (SIU), the province's police watchdog agency, cleared Mercey, finding he had no choice but to shoot Preston or be killed himself.
The five-member inquest jury will examine the events surrounding the deaths and make recommendations to ensure a similar tragedy doesn't happen again in future.
Mercey will be the key witness, the only of the three men to survive the situation he said "simply went bad."
It began when Preston drove from Sunridge, north of Huntsville, to his sister-in-law's home, looking for his ex-wife. No one was home, but Preston called his daughter who then contacted police.
Preston was carrying his hunting rifle. He approached Pham, a 37-year-old father of three, raised the gun and pulled the trigger.
Preston began firing as he walked towards Mercey, who took cover between his cruiser and the side of the road.
By the time it was over, Preston was lying on the side of the road with six bullet holes in him. He died days later in a London hospital.
The inquest, expected to last 13 days, will finally close this chapter of Mersey's life. In April, he'll leave the force for good when he officially retires, though his final shift was in January.
"I've moved on pretty good," he said. "It happened and, you know, there's nothing you can do about it. That's just the way life is and you've got to move on."
